standard_prerequisites.use: They keep flatness after the etale base change, transfer it to the new base, translate the devissage into the affine-algebra statement, and then conclude projectivity of the module over the new base after replacing it by a standard open neighbourhood.

core_obligations: Reduce to the flat case: by openness of flatness one may replace the source by an open neighbourhood of the point and assume the module is flat over the base (proof lines 3310-3314).

Get the devissage after an etale neighbourhood: apply the existence statement to obtain the diagram of pointed schemes with elementary etale horizontal arrows over which the pulled back module has a complete devissage at the lifted point (proof lines 3314-3318).

Conclude: the pulled back module is still flat over the base and, by the up and down lemma, flat over the new base; the affine description translates the devissage into the corresponding statement about the module of global sections, so the finite presentation devissage statement gives the result after replacing the new base by a standard open neighbourhood (proof lines 3319-3334).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a flat module on a neighbourhood (proof lines 3310-3314).
Apply the existence of a devissage after an etale neighbourhood (proof lines 3314-3318).
Transfer flatness and apply the devissage statement (proof lines 3319-3334).
difficulty_reason: The proposition produces, for a finitely presented module flat at a point of a locally finitely presented morphism, a diagram of pointed schemes with elementary etale horizontal arrows and affine vertices on which the global sections of the pulled back module are projective (statement lines 3286-3308, tag 05I6-adjacent). The proof reduces to a flat module on a neighbourhood by openness of flatness, invokes the existence of a complete devissage after an elementary etale neighbourhood, keeps flatness through the base change and transfers it to the new base by the up and down lemma, and then applies the finite presentation devissage statement to conclude projectivity. The transfer of flatness and the translation into the affine statement are the substance, so the claim is H2.
